title: X Feed Digest
summary: Major model updates continue: Gemini 3 Deep Think rolled out new reasoning capabilities while ByteDance’s Seed 2 Pro is being positioned as a frontier‑level multimodal contender with aggressive pricing.

Developer tooling is accelerating toward agent‑first workflows, with Claude Code shipping meaningful CLI fixes and big performance gains, and OpenAI documenting a Codex‑driven, zero‑hand‑code product build.
The WebMCP spec from Google/Microsoft could turn websites into structured agent APIs, shifting optimization from SEO to agent‑experience design.
Markets are in focus with a heavy earnings week, a slightly softer‑than‑expected CPI print, and fresh debate on Microsoft’s OpenAI exposure plus rising AMC short interest.

items.title: @GeminiApp: Gemini 3 Deep Think upgrade
items.body: Google rolled out a major upgrade to Gemini 3 Deep Think, positioning it for practical reasoning workflows like modeling physical systems. The demo highlights turning a sketch into a 3D‑printable model, now rolling out to AI Ultra subscribers.

items.title: @ClaudeCodeLog: Claude Code 2.1.41
items.body: The CLI update adds explicit auth login/status/logout commands, Windows ARM64 native builds, and a timeout to prevent AWS auth refresh hangs. It also improves /rename auto‑naming and fixes multiple UI/IO bugs.

items.title: @jarredsumner: Claude Code Bash speedup
items.body: An upcoming Claude Code release makes the Bash tool dramatically faster and lighter—benchmark drops from 115s to 15s when streaming 10GB to stdout (~7× faster). That’s a big win for heavy shell output workloads.

items.title: @aakashgupta: WebMCP turns sites into agent APIs
items.body: Google and Microsoft co‑authored WebMCP, a browser API (navigator.modelContext) that lets sites expose structured tools directly to agents. Early claims suggest ~67% less compute with ~98% task accuracy, pushing optimization toward agent‑experience design.

items.title: @shao__meng: OpenAI’s agent‑first engineering
items.body: OpenAI’s engineering blog describes a Codex‑driven workflow where 3 engineers produced ~1M lines and ~1,500 PRs in five months with zero hand‑written code. The emphasis is on environment design, strict repo structure, and feedback loops as the real leverage.

items.title: @deedydas: ByteDance Seed 2 Pro
items.body: ByteDance’s Seed 2 Pro is framed as a breakthrough multimodal model, claiming top‑tier image/video understanding and near‑frontier general performance. Pricing is highlighted as lower than Gemini Flash ($0.47/M input, $2.37/M output), signaling aggressive competition.

items.title: @Stocktwits: Earnings‑heavy week
items.body: A packed earnings calendar lands Tuesday–Friday with major names like PANW, CDNS, WMT, BABA, BKNG, and others; Monday is a market holiday. Useful for planning event‑driven moves.

items.title: @Scswga: CPI slightly below expectations
items.body: A reposted CPI update reports headline CPI at 2.4% vs 2.5% expected, while core CPI matched expectations at 2.5%. The read adds a modestly dovish note to near‑term Fed narratives.

items.title: @aakashgupta: Microsoft underperformance vs peers
items.body: Commentary flags MSFT down ~27% from its October high while the S&P hits new highs, tying the gap to OpenAI concentration risk (45% of remaining obligations). It also highlights heavy capex and margin pressure as investor concerns.

items.title: @S3Partners: AMC short interest spikes
items.body: Short sellers re‑engaged AMC after dilution approval, pushing short interest to multi‑year highs. Borrow tightening and high utilization suggest higher volatility and potential recall/covering risk.

items.title: @runes_leo: Old PC → TikTok AI agent
items.body: A longform case study shows an unused gaming PC turned into an AI agent that auto‑produces TikTok content—scaling from sub‑1k views to 500k in five days. The author documents each iteration and fix, making it a practical playbook.

items.title: @scaling_shields: Quiet $2.8k/mo phone‑answering biz
items.body: A solo operator reportedly built a $1.9M/year service answering calls for storage facilities at $2.8k/month. The insight: boring, recurring problems with high LTV and low churn can beat flashy, visible products.
